claim: LACIE frames confidence calibration as preference optimization (DPO) rather than reward-shaped RL, generating training data via a two-agent speaker-listener game where a simulated listener judges whether the speaker's answer plus confidence should be accepted.
stance_target: DPO/preference optimization is a viable alternative to RL reward-shaping for training expressed confidence
quoted_support: We cast calibration as preference optimization, creating data via a two-agent game, where a speaker model's outputs are judged by a simulated listener.

claim: In human evaluation, LACIE-trained models led to 47% fewer incorrect answers being accepted by human listeners while maintaining the same acceptance rate for correct answers -- a discrimination-relevant, decision-theoretic result beyond standard ECE/AUROC.
stance_target: training-time calibration can be validated by downstream human decision quality, not just statistical metrics
scope_conditions: human annotators evaluating LLM answers post LACIE fine-tuning
quoted_support: Training with LACIE results in 47% fewer incorrect answers being accepted while maintaining the same level of acceptance for correct answers.

claim: LACIE calibrates both explicit confidence markers (numeric scores) and implicit markers (authoritative tone, hedging, elaboration), and analysis shows LACIE-trained models hedge more and signal certainty through tone/detail when correct, plus emergent increased abstention on likely-wrong answers.
stance_target: an expressed confidence interface can include implicit linguistic markers, not just a single numeric token
scope_conditions: qualitative analysis of LACIE-trained model outputs
quoted_support: A LACIE-trained model hedges more and implicitly signals certainty when it is correct by using an authoritative tone or including details... LACIE finetuning leads to an emergent increase in model abstention.

claim: LACIE generalizes from TriviaQA training to a large increase in truthfulness on TruthfulQA, and its analysis indicates it produces better confidence separation between correct and incorrect examples (a discrimination-type claim).
stance_target: DPO-trained verbalized confidence can generalize out-of-domain and be discriminative
scope_conditions: TriviaQA-trained model evaluated zero-shot on TruthfulQA
quoted_support: LACIE generalizes to another dataset, resulting in a large increase in truthfulness on TruthfulQA when trained on TriviaQA. Our analysis indicates that LACIE leads to a better confidence separation between correct and incorrect examples.
